hints: Focus on how Period 3 oxides and chlorides change from ionic to covalent, and what that means for reaction with water.
The first two clues point to the left side of Period 3, since only Na and Mg have giant ionic oxides and chlorides that simply dissolve without giving HCl fumes.
For Y, list melting points across Period 3 and ask which element is second lowest after argon, then pair it with X to check the options.
walkthrough:
**Use the oxide clue to narrow down X**

Think of Period 3 oxides from left to right. $\text{Na}_2\text{O}$, $\text{MgO}$, $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{SiO}_2$ are all solids with giant structures (ionic or macromolecular).

$$\text{P}_4\text{O}_{10}, \text{SO}_2, \text{Cl}_2\text{O} \text{ are simple molecular}$$ 
So X must be one of Na, Mg, Al, Si.

**Use the chloride clue to pin down X further**

Now think about chlorides with water. Covalent chlorides like $\text{AlCl}_3$, $\text{SiCl}_4$ and $\text{PCl}_5$ hydrolyse vigorously to give acidic solutions and white fumes of $\text{HCl}$.

Ionic chlorides like $\text{NaCl}$ just dissolve to a neutral solution with no reaction, and $\text{MgCl}_2$ dissolves with only very slight hydrolysis. So X must be from the far left, Na or Mg.

**Identify Y from melting points**

Recall the melting point trend in Period 3. Silicon is highest, then Al and Mg are high, while Na, P, S, Cl are low and Ar (monatomic gas) is lowest.

In order: $\text{Ar} < \text{Cl} < \text{P} < \text{Na} < \text{S} < \text{Mg} < \text{Al} < \text{Si}$. The only element with just argon below it is chlorine. So Y is Cl.

**Combine X and Y**

We have X as Na or Mg, and Y as Cl. A compound of Na and Cl is $\text{NaCl}$, with $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions in a 1:1 ratio.

This matches one of the given formulae, so that must be the possible compound.

options.A: Al2S3 would need X = Al and Y = S. Al is ruled out because AlCl3 reacts vigorously with water, and S is ruled out because Na, P and Cl all melt lower than S, not just argon.
options.B: MgS would need X = Mg and Y = S. Mg fits the X clues, but Y cannot be S because S has a melting point around 115 C, which is higher than Na, P and Cl as well as Ar.
options.C: NaCl fits perfectly. Na has a giant ionic oxide (Na2O) and its chloride simply dissolves with no hydrolysis reaction. Cl fits Y because it has the second lowest melting point in Period 3 after Ar.
options.D: PCl5 would need X = P and Y = Cl. Y = Cl is correct, but X cannot be P because the oxide of P is simple molecular, not giant, and PCl5 hydrolyses vigorously with water.
